name: Antigua and Barbuda
summary_text: Antigua and Barbuda demands real caution. The High Court struck down the buggery/gross-indecency laws in July 2022, reading the constitutional bar on sex discrimination to cover sexual orientation and gender identity. No LGR, no anti-discrimination statute, and residual social hostility; tourist resort areas are insulated.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust page documents constitutional challenges to laws criminalising same-sex activity across the Eastern Caribbean, including Antigua and Barbuda.

sources.title: Antigua and Barbuda: High Court Decriminalizes Gay Sex | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Jul 2022): 'Antigua and Barbuda: High Court Decriminalizes Gay Sex' — the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court strikes down the 'sodomy' and 'gross indecency' provisions.

sources.title: Antigua and Barbuda | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): in 2022 the High Court found Sections 12 and 15 of the Sexual Offences Act 1995 unconstitutional, decriminalising same-sex conduct, and interpreted 'sex' discrimination to include sexual orientation and gender identity. However, no explicit antidiscrimination protections exist, same-sex unions are not recognised, and trans people are particularly vulnerable because there is no mechanism to change legal gender markers - only name changes.

ILGA 'State-Sponsored Homophobia' world survey (May 2009): global survey of laws prohibiting same-sex activity between consenting adults, with per-country entries including Antigua and Barbuda (then criminalising buggery and gross indecency).

sources.title: Orden David: Meet the LGBTQ activist who challenged his Caribbean country’s anti-sodomy law and won | International | EL PAÍS English
sources.claim_summary: El País/AP (June 2023): profile of Orden David, the Antiguan LGBTQ activist who challenged the country's anti-sodomy law and won in 2022 - he had been bullied and physically attacked (struck in the head, knocked out in daylight); the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court ruled the law unconstitutional; six Caribbean countries still criminalise.

sources.title: ECADE: ‘Draconian’ buggery and indecency laws soon to be challenged in court! | THE STAR - St Lucia
sources.claim_summary: St Lucia Star (Dec 2019): ECADE announced court challenges to buggery and indecency laws in Barbados, St Kitts-Nevis, Antigua and Barbuda, Grenada and Saint Lucia, arguing the laws stigmatise and legitimise hate speech, discrimination and violence.
The Advocates for Human Rights: submission for Antigua and Barbuda before the UN Human Rights Committee (suggested list of issues prior to reporting), covering LGBTQ+ rights.
